{
  "final_quality": "tie",
  "reason": "Both support the same consequential outcome: retain the characterized adapter on private staging, publish atomically, preserve unrelated SKUs, make retries idempotent, and require actual CLI, invalid-record, interruption and recovery tests during implementation. A adopts COMMIT as an explicit boundary assumption; B retains compatible interruption semantics as a condition on implementation. Neither claims product acceptance. Their different staging mechanisms, probe coverage and review detail do not demonstrate a material final-quality advantage.",
  "decisive_evidence": [
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "snapshot existing database read-only to private stage, real adapter.apply there, then one explicit destination transaction for complete inventory copy.",
      "locator": "A.plans[0].final.work_items[W2].context",
      "consequence": "Isolates the adapter's row commits and publishes a complete inventory snapshot that preserves unrelated SKUs."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "Existing DB uses explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus staged-row transfer then one commit; absent path uses closed complete stage file replacement.",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.work_items[W2].context",
      "consequence": "Provides a credible atomic publication route for existing and initially absent destinations without replacing a live WAL database."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "All new feature acceptance remains due after implementation.",
      "locator": "A.planning_artifacts: run/notes/plan.md, Design basis",
      "consequence": "The feasibility observation and passing baseline do not substitute for product acceptance."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "A3/A4 are probed primitives, not product success.",
      "locator": "B.plans[0].final.work_items[W2].context",
      "consequence": "Transaction and replacement observations remain distinct from the unimplemented importer, CLI and recovery checks."
    },
    {
      "side": "A",
      "quote": "Precommit interruption exposes B; postcommit interruption exposes complete S with safe retry.",
      "locator": "A.planning_artifacts: docs/shiploop/architecture.md, AD-6",
      "consequence": "Explicitly acknowledges the commit/acknowledgement limitation instead of claiming that postcommit death restores old inventory."
    },
    {
      "side": "B",
      "quote": "The planning trial can stop at prepare with this gap visible, without asserting product readiness.",
      "locator": "B.planning_artifacts: run/notes/batch-plan.md, Evaluated primitive decisions and implementation recovery obligations",
      "consequence": "The unresolved interpretation is an explicit implementation condition, not hidden false readiness or an abandoned requirement."
    }
  ],
  "initial_plan_and_rework": "A's initial plan already contained the consequential architecture, helper-first ordering, independent state oracles and deferred acceptance. Review added an explicit graph dependency already present in W3 prose and a concrete helper-suite selector; these improve usability without repairing the core design. B's initial plan already selected transactional publication and an absent-path replacement branch conditionally. Review supplied the promised primitive observations, clarified batch-only staging, strengthened ownership and SQLite-sidecar cleanup constraints, and specified the helper interface. Those are useful refinements and uncertainty reduction, particularly for B's chosen cleanup behavior, but do not show that its initial architecture was unsound. B underwent more substantive review work; that is separate from comparative final quality.",
  "earlier_evidence_value": "The supplied matching-source adapter evidence was already sufficient to exclude direct visible writes while retaining the adapter privately. Both reused it legitimately; hash validation, source inspection and baseline checks were appropriate. Their later probes addressed separate publication questions rather than repeating the characterized invalid-record experiment. A obtained its mechanism observation before the initial plan; B explicitly deferred primitive confirmation to review. Neither timing nor experiment count establishes superiority. The baseline proves only the existing single-row behavior, and all new feature acceptance remains due.",
  "harms_or_lost_requirements": [],
  "individual_judgment_corrections": [
    "B's individual judgment treats the acknowledgement clarification gate as necessarily unnecessary. The request combines unchanged inventory after interruption with complete successful publication without explicitly defining the acknowledgement interval. B preserves that ambiguity conditionally; the record shows no actual clarification exchange, implementation delay or waived requirement. The claimed disadvantage is therefore not demonstrated.",
    "B's individual wording about observing prior state 'before commit' needs a narrow reading. In tx_probe.py, observe() runs after the child terminates, and the held reader is closed first. This establishes rollback after precommit termination, not a fresh-reader observation while the writer remains paused. It does not invalidate the publication plan.",
    "No clear factual contradiction appears in A's individual judgment's core adapter, architecture or deferred-acceptance findings. Its distinction between substantive decisions and graph/selector clarification is supported by the initial work-item contracts."
  ],
  "confidence": "medium",
  "limits": [
    "Neither outcome implements the importer, CLI or retained fault fixture. Planning completion and the passing baseline are not release or feature-acceptance evidence.",
    "A's completed-stage retry and new-destination snapshot copy do not establish actual CLI recovery or a fresh J-only import. B's selected transaction and replacement boundaries do not establish every interruption timing or power-loss behavior.",
    "The omitted command transcript is needed to independently resolve A's alleged repeated framework reads and other event-specific overhead claims. These remain unresolved cost observations, not demonstrated correctness regressions.",
    "B's unresolved user-intent boundary cannot be settled experimentally; A's documented boundary default is not evidence of explicit user agreement. External endpoints are outside the supplied scope, not verified capabilities.",
    "Both records report seed preservation and child/database cleanup. Retained scripts and evidence files provide no demonstrated sensitive-data, authority, running-resource or inventory harm."
  ]
}
requested_model_attestation: Exact model and effort requested; provider served identity not independently exposed.
